**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `e8bab4e71ad22a2bf4e061a05480dd341ca0e564`.

Light whole-PR review against `ae8e7ee24dbce1ca5c57e9e333c8a5424fc9f11e`. The bind resolver accepts port0 using the same SocketAddr parse, without adding a process, query, worker or timer. Default bind stays `127.0.0.1:7461`; client-address validation is unchanged.

**P188-N001, launch-count correction:** the removed Node `createServer().listen(0)` and Rust `TcpListener::bind(...:0)` reserved ports **inside their existing test processes**. Neither launched a child. Each fixture now avoids one temporary reservation listener/bind-close lifecycle; its existing daemon child remains. Direct process-launch count is unchanged, not reduced by one.

The OS atomically selects a port during the daemon's existing bind, removing the reserve-close-rebind race. Both fixtures consume the existing listening banner; Node already waited for that banner and Rust adds a nonzero-port assertion inside its existing poll. Readiness deadlines/cadence are unchanged. Avoiding failed/retried tests may save work, but no retry-rate or latency saving was measured.

**Exact-head CI:** [42471751206](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42471751206), successful Rust job `128705210957` on attempt2, upload artifact **13614275297**: **2,237 executed cases passed**, zero failures/errors, five separately skipped. The daemon-log integration case verifies a real nonzero bound address; all six spawn guards pass. Node22's job log executes **all 16 inbox integration cases** against the private Rust daemon, whose setup rejects port0/production7461 in the banner and checks health. Node22/24, Rust lint and delivers checks succeed.

Worktree/GitHub heads agree, clean and CLEAN. No local daemon, listener reservation, build, test, mutation or performance probe was run.
